formatNotes: First year of the modern three-stage season: the worldwide Open (over 26,000 athletes, six weekly workouts) fed 17 Regionals, which qualified roughly 50 athletes per division to the Games. First year of the Reebok title sponsorship ('Reebok CrossFit Games') and a $250,000 first-place prize. Each event was worth 100 points to the winner; points dropped 5 per place through 6th (95, 90, 85, 80, 75), then 2 per place from 7th through 30th, then 1 per place beyond. Progressive cuts during the weekend: the official leaderboard shows 48 of 49 men and 45 of 47 women scored Event 1, and 47 men / 45 women scored Events 2-5 (not quite the full field: Rob Orlando was DNF in the swim, Mikko Salo withdrew after it with a burst eardrum, and Deborah Cordner Carson and Helga Torfadottir went unscored from Event 1 on); 35 men and 35 women contested Event 6 (Killer Kage), 24 contested Event 7 (Dog-Sled), and the final 12 per division contested Events 8-10 (The End 1-3). Note: Wikipedia phrases the cuts as coming 'after the 6th event' and 'after the 7th'; the leaderboard's scored-athlete counts (35 in Event 6, 24 in Event 7, 12 in Events 8-10) are recorded here as authoritative.
yearSummary: 2011 was the year the CrossFit Games became a season: the inaugural Open and Regionals funneled a true worldwide field into Carson, Reebok signed on as title sponsor, ESPN3 streamed the weekend, and the champions' checks jumped to $250,000. Dave Castro leaned into 'unknown and unknowable' programming - the Games opened off-site with an ocean swim event at Santa Monica beach (where 2009 champion Mikko Salo burst an eardrum and withdrew), and skills tests (softball throw, handstand walk, L-sit, max weighted pull-up, water-jug carry) plus new implements (Watt bikes, the Kage monkey-bar rig, the Rogue dog sled) debuted alongside classic barbell work. Rich Froning, the 2010 runner-up, won three events and avenged his 2010 rope-climb collapse by winning Rope-Clean, claiming the first of his four straight titles; Iceland's Annie Thorisdottir won three events herself to take the women's crown from Kristan Clever. Josh Bridges (men) and Sam Briggs (women) each won multiple events, and the weekend ended with The End, a three-part repeated chipper finale capped by a rope-assisted sled pull.

events.name: Beach
events.description:
For time:
210-meter ocean swim
1,500-meter soft-sand run
50 chest-to-bar pull-ups
100 hand-release push-ups
200 squats
1,500-meter soft-sand run

Same distances and reps for men and women. Contested off-site on the beach at Santa Monica: athletes swam out and around buoys in the ocean, ran 1,500 m down the soft sand, completed the pull-ups on temporary rigs, the push-ups and air squats on the beach, then ran 1,500 m back to the finish.
events.notes: First swim event in Games history and the first individual event held away from the main venue. 2009 champion Mikko Salo burst an eardrum during the ocean swim and withdrew from the competition. Navy SEAL Josh Bridges won the men's heat.

events.name: Skills 1
events.description:
Three tests:
1. Max L-sit for time (1 attempt)
2. Max-distance softball throw (2 attempts)
3. Max-distance handstand walk (1 attempt, with 1 mulligan if less than 5 yards)

Same tests for men and women, no external loading. Athletes were ranked in each test, and the sum of their three rankings determined their finish for the event (low sum wins); the event then paid out the standard 100-point scale like every other event.
events.notes: First of two ranked-skills events, part of 2011's 'unknown and unknowable' theme. Component-by-component results were not preserved on the official leaderboard, which records only final event points; the winning scores shown are event points, not raw marks.

events.name: Rope-Clean
events.description:
For time:
15-foot rope climb, 5 ascents
Clean and jerks, 5 reps (145 lb M / 115 lb W)
15-foot rope climb, 4 ascents
Clean and jerks, 4 reps (165 lb M / 125 lb W)
15-foot rope climb, 3 ascents
Clean and jerks, 3 reps (185 lb M / 135 lb W)
15-foot rope climb, 2 ascents
Clean and jerks, 2 reps (205 lb M / 145 lb W)
15-foot rope climb, 1 ascent
Clean and jerk, 1 rep (225 lb M / 155 lb W)

Descending 5-4-3-2-1 couplet: 15 total rope ascents and 15 total clean and jerks, with the barbell load climbing 20 lb (men) / 10 lb (women) each round.
events.notes: Friday night stadium event. Rich Froning, whose inability to climb a rope cost him the 2010 title, won the event outright; both eventual champions (Froning and Thorisdottir) won it in their divisions.

events.name: Triplet Sprint
events.description:
For time:
5 muscle-ups
10 deadlifts (245 lb M / 165 lb W)
15 GHD sit-ups
Sprint 50 yards
5 muscle-ups
10 deadlifts (245 lb M / 165 lb W)
15 GHD sit-ups
Sprint 100 yards
5 muscle-ups
10 deadlifts (245 lb M / 165 lb W)
15 GHD sit-ups
Sprint 150 yards
5 muscle-ups
10 deadlifts (245 lb M / 165 lb W)
15 GHD sit-ups
Sprint 200 yards

Four rounds of the muscle-up/deadlift/GHD triplet, with the sprint growing by 50 yards each round (500 yards of running total).

events.name: Skills 2
events.description:
Three tests:
1. 1-rep-max weighted chest-to-bar pull-up for load (2 minutes to establish)
2. 1-rep-max snatch for load (2 minutes to establish)
3. Jug carry for distance in 60 seconds (carry 2 weighted steel 5-gallon water jugs as far as possible)

Athletes were ranked in each test, and the sum of their three rankings determined their finish for the event (low sum wins), paying out the standard 100-point scale.
events.notes: The weight of the steel water jugs was never published on the official card. Documented component bests, all per the official Event 5 results article (games.crossfit.com/article/2011-games-individual-event-5-results): Lucas Parker's 130-lb weighted chest-to-bar pull-up (men), Lindsay Valenzuela's 165-lb snatch (women), and Elisabeth Akinwale's 364-ft jug carry (women's farthest; the article reads '364 feet even - and she turned around at the end of the field and walked back'). Winning scores shown are event points, not raw marks; the leaderboard preserved only final event placings.

events.name: Killer Kage
events.description:
Three rounds for time of:
7 front squats (225 lb M / 155 lb W)
Bike 700 meters
100-foot monkey bar traverse

Barbell taken from the ground. Athletes rode bikes on a 700-meter loop out of the stadium and back each round, then crossed the 100-foot 'Kage' monkey-bar rig.
events.notes: Saturday night event. First time bikes were used at the Games and debut of the 'Kage' monkey-bar rig. First post-cut event: only the top 35 men and 35 women contested it.

events.name: Dog-Sled
events.description:
For time:
Three rounds of:
30 double-unders
10 overhead squats (135 lb M / 95 lb W)
then, three rounds of:
10 handstand push-ups
40-foot sled push (sled + 385 lb M / sled + 275 lb W)

Back-to-back couplets: three rounds of the double-under/overhead-squat couplet, immediately followed by three rounds of handstand push-ups and a 40-foot push of a heavily loaded dog sled.
events.notes: Debut of the Rogue dog sled at the Games. Contested by the final 24 men and 24 women after the second cut.

events.name: The End 1
events.description:
Complete as many reps as possible in 3 minutes of:
20-calorie row
30 wall-ball shots (20-lb ball M / 14-lb ball W)
20 toes-to-bars
30 box jumps (24-inch box, men and women)
20 sumo deadlift high pulls (108-lb kettlebell M / 72-lb kettlebell W)
30 burpees
20 shoulder-to-overheads (135 lb M / 95 lb W)
Sled pull

First part of the three-part finale: athletes worked through the chipper from the top for 3 minutes, scored by total reps completed. 1 minute of rest before The End 2.
events.notes: Contested by the final 12 men and 12 women only. The End 1, 2 and 3 were three separately scored 100-point events run nearly back to back. Box height was 24 inches for both divisions. The closing sled pull's load and distance were never published on the official card; athletes pulled a sled in hand over hand by rope.

events.name: The End 2
events.description:
Complete as many reps as possible in 6 minutes of:
20-calorie row
30 wall-ball shots (20-lb ball M / 14-lb ball W)
20 toes-to-bars
30 box jumps (24-inch box, men and women)
20 sumo deadlift high pulls (108-lb kettlebell M / 72-lb kettlebell W)
30 burpees
20 shoulder-to-overheads (135 lb M / 95 lb W)
Sled pull

Second part of the finale, begun after 1 minute of rest: athletes restarted the same chipper from the top and worked for 6 minutes, scored by total reps completed. 2 minutes of rest before The End 3.
events.notes: Contested by the final 12 men and 12 women only. Each part restarted the chipper from the beginning rather than continuing from the previous stopping point.

events.name: The End 3
events.description:
For time:
20-calorie row
30 wall-ball shots (20-lb ball M / 14-lb ball W)
20 toes-to-bars
30 box jumps (24-inch box, men and women)
20 sumo deadlift high pulls (108-lb kettlebell M / 72-lb kettlebell W)
30 burpees
20 shoulder-to-overheads (135 lb M / 95 lb W)
Sled pull

Third and final part, begun after 2 minutes of rest: the complete chipper for time, finishing with the rope-assisted sled pull across the stadium floor. First athlete to finish the eight stations won the event and the 2011 season ended at the sled.
events.notes: Contested by the final 12 men and 12 women only. Rich Froning (8th, 14:10) and Annie Thorisdottir (3rd, 13:56) protected their leads through the finale to win their first titles. Froning called the closing sled pull the most miserable part of the weekend: 'I had no core left, no arms left.'
